70.prompt: Back on February 9, 2026 Leonard put a cash and liabilities snapshot on the list of things the wind-down needs, and nobody has written it, so I told him I'd draft it while he stays on the lawyers and the dissolution paperwork. Please write it up as a memo for him, built from what actually happened rather than from forecast numbers: what we still owe (including anything with a hard date on it), what is owed to us, where cash stands (the most recent actual bank balance Leonard put a date on, plus anything he has estimated since), and every payment the bank notified us it processed since September 1, 2025, by month and by who it went to. A lot of this moved in the last few weeks, so go by the latest word on each item and say so where something that looked owed, or owed to us, no longer is. Share the memo with Leonard and Arthur, post the link in the wind-down channel, and give me the headline numbers here.

golden.golden_answer:
Position as of February 13, 2026, built from invoices, bank notices, vendor and advisor emails and the founders' Slack channels. No forecast numbers are used.
 
Still owed. Singular: invoice INVSINC23580 (Dec 1, 2025) for $6,250.00, overdue per its Jan 5, 2026 notice. On Jan 15, 2026 Singular extended the due date to March 15, 2026. On Feb 10, 2026 in #executives Leonard listed what has to be paid: Singular $18,750, Unity about $2,348 a month for 9 months, and Helpshift $150 a month for 8 months. So his figure for Singular is $18,750. He emailed a termination notice on Feb 12, 2026 saying no funds remain; no reply. The earlier invoice INVSINC22671 is not open, the bank paid it on Sept 26, 2025. Unity: about $2,348 a month for 9 months, roughly $21,100, still unresolved on Feb 12, 2026 when Leonard drafts the termination note for Arthur. Deel: two approval requests on Feb 11, 2026, $4,500.00 and $5,100.00, total $9,600.00 pending. SVB credit card: about $8,000 ($8.5K on Jan 22, $8K on Jan 23, 2026), to be paid off and closed once the data money arrives. Hard dates: the Delaware franchise tax filing is due March 1, 2026. This is in Robert's own mailbox, in the thread "Re: 2025 DE Franchise Tax", where the accountant wrote on Feb 11, 2026 (21:00 UTC) that missing "the filing deadline of March 1st" means penalties and interest. Both games must be off Helpshift before February 28, 2026.
 
Looked owed, no longer is. Helpshift: $1,500 on Feb 9 (#winddown), restated as $150 a month for 8 months on Feb 10 (#executives), then in #admin_foundersonly that day Leonard wrote "All outstanding Helpshift is paid", $300 from his own pocket. Paid in full Feb 10, 2026, not a company liability. Deel overdue notice of $9,717.90 (Feb 2, 2026): cleared by the $9,889.90 bank payment to Deel the same day. Law firm: a $715 review charge raised Feb 11, 2026 in #executives was removed and discounted 100% in the "engagement Letter Material" thread.
 
Owed to the company. Data purchase: $22,500.00 all-cash offer on Feb 12, 2026, not yet received. ironSource: payable balance of $520.82 quoted Nov 24, 2025; ticket closed Dec 15, 2025 with nothing paid; still uncollected. No longer owed to us: the federal R&D tax credit of $24,275 looked like incoming cash on Feb 10, 2026, but the accountant said it can only offset payroll tax the company no longer has. Not collectible now.
 
Cash. The most recent actual balance Leonard dated is $25,031 as of 01/11/2026 ("Actual balance as of 01/11/2026: 25031", HG P&L tab, Harmony Games P&L and forecast - Jan 2026). The $52,686.59 he gave the accountants is as of 12/31/2025, so it is older. His latest estimate is about $4K (Jan 30, 2026, #executives). The warehouse cash table (25,010 at Jan 31, 2026) is not Leonard's figure and is not used.
 
Bank payments. 21 "SVB Payment Notification: Payment Processed" emails from Sept 1, 2025 to Feb 13, 2026; awaiting-approval and scheduled notices are excluded. By month in USD: Sept 2025 $57,403.46; Oct $47,205.06; Nov $4,144.22; Dec $28,799.68; Jan 2026 $27,576.03; Feb $17,309.90. Total $182,438.35 across 20 USD payments. One Oct 30, 2025 payment of 1,999.00 BGN is not in dollars and is reported separately. By payee: Deel $133,444.13 (5 payments: 43,733.46, 39,285.06, 20,879.68, 19,656.03, 9,889.90; the Sept 30 notice masks the name and matches Deel by account ending 8380); Eveline Art S.R.L. $18,600.00 (5 x 3,720.00); Leapblock LTD $18,500.00 (5 x 3,700.00); Singular Labs $6,250.00; AppLovin $4,144.22 (Nov 12, 2025); individual payee with account ending 5384 $1,500.00 (3 x 500.00). Both breakdowns total $182,438.35.
 
Actions. The memo is a Google Doc shared with leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co and arthur.blake@harmonygames.co, with the link posted in #winddown. The reply to Robert gives the headline numbers: Singular $6,250.00 due March 15, 2026 ($18,750 by Leonard's count), Unity about $21,100, Deel $9,600.00 pending, card about $8,000, Delaware March 1, 2026, owed to us $22,500.00 and $520.82, R&D credit not collectible, cash $25,031 on Jan 11, 2026 and about $4K on Jan 30, bank payments $182,438.35.
 
Not graded: the wind-down provider's fee, since the records give about $15K, then $11,700, then "slightly higher", with no final figure.

71.prompt:
We're shutting the company down and I keep putting off the one thing that actually bothers me. Both games are still live, people are still playing them, and I genuinely don't know what's still running inside domino delights. There's a whole schedule of live events somewhere that nobody's touched since December, and I have no idea which of those things are actually firing right now versus stopped months ago. I've heard both. Support goes dark on February 28, 2026 and after that nobody's answering players at all.
Can you work out what's actually live in domino delights and zombie match right now, and give me a plan for what we do about each of it before the end of the month? I care most about anything players can spend money on, and anything that's going to start up on its own after we're gone. For each thing tell me whether it stays or goes dark, when it has to happen by, and who has to do it and be straight with me about what we can't get done in time. I'd rather know now than find out from a player. Arthur's the only one left who can touch the backend, and he's not around much longer.
Also the roadmap boards are a mess, there's stuff sitting on them that looks live and isn't, and the other way round. Once you know the real state, fix the records so whoever picks this up after us isn't working off fiction

golden.golden_answer:
Both games are fully live and everything in them is still running. Warehouse telemetry shows every catalogued event firing through the February 9, 2026 cutoff. That contradicts the Confluence Live-Ops Event Engine page, which says the July 2025 outage took Domino events dark and was never marked restored, and the wind-down claim that live ops died in summer. The Live-Ops Event Calendar page, self-described as the single source of truth, was updated January 31, 2026 and still carries that stale framing.
Domino Delights has six recurring events live: Win & Collect, Weekly Quests, Weekly Leaderboards, River Rush, Axe Arena, Streak Fever. Plus a Season Pass, in game-of-dominoes-backend at lib/NodeJsFargateApiStack.ts: SeasonPassesAddRule fires a lambda on cron 0 0 1 * * writing a season-pass record with a 365-day TTL, route at /season-pass in server.js. It opens a new purchasable season on March 1, 2026. The coin store is selling: of 63 real-money items in tools/catalog-items.json, 12 are Available and DisplayInStore, reaching $99.99. The other 51 are Available with DisplayInStore false, hidden but not blocked server-side, including the Enchanted Starter Pack at $0.99, three Remove Ads tiers at $0.99, $2.99 and $4.99, and bundle.tier7.seasonpass at $6.99. All purchases are one-time, no subscriptions, so nothing auto-bills. Domino reward tables are static JS in libs/rewards-data/ with no Sheets dependency; its Sheets ingestion is liveops/quests/lambda/ingestor.js, covering quests, chests and achievements, on an 8-hour schedule.
The plan runs through Arthur before February 20, 2026. Both Season Passes first, the only purchasable products opening unattended on March 1. Then the coin store, visible and hidden SKUs together, which sells until a deploy stops it and whose refunds are unanswerable after February 28. Then the recurring events across all four stacks, naming each Zombie Match system: Leagues, Endless Monster Mode, Boss Arena, Win & Collect, Plague Race. Confirm with Arthur which Google account authenticates both quests ingestors, since the company-wide February 15, 2026 account deletion deadline likely breaks that Sheets import, then fix or accept it.
What can't be done in time: no in-app shutdown notice, since that needs a client build through store review; no refund path after February 28; and no way to confirm from backend source alone whether the hidden season-pass SKU is reachable.
Records to correct: the Event Engine page's claim that Domino has been dark since July 2025; the Event Calendar table, which shows Weekly Quests as failed in November 2024 when it has run through February 2026, and omits Leagues and Boss Arena; the Cappadocia (February) cards on DD Product Roadmap calling River Rush, Streak Fever and Season Pass spec-ready when all three are live; the ZM ROADMAP board, whose dated lists stop at Nov 5 while the game has kept shipping; and ART-73 and DES-9, orphaned open under the cancelled EPI-2 epic.
golden.alternative_approaches_notes:
The golden solution turns things off by deploying changed CDK stacks. A direct database edit is equally valid. The Confluence live-ops engine page names both routes explicitly, and the July 2025 outage was resolved by hand in the database rather than by a deploy, so there's precedent for it in the universe. Either way the work still has to go through Arthur before February 20, 2026, so the deadline and the owner don't change.
Sequencing can differ too. The golden solution kills both Season Pass crons first because they're the only purchasable things that open unattended on March 1. An answer that stops all the recurring events in the same deploy window, rather than staging the passes ahead of the rest, is fine as long as everything lands before February 20 and the passes are covered.
The coin store is a genuine judgment call rather than a fixed answer. Leaving it selling until the apps come down, and disabling it before support ends, are both defensible. What matters is that the answer picks one, says why, and is honest that refunds can't be serviced after February 28.
Unpublishing the store listings is a valid addition but not a valid substitute. Installed clients keep talking to the backend, so the passes still open on March 1 whether or not the listings are up. An answer recommending removal alongside the backend changes is fine; one recommending it instead of them has missed the mechanism.
On the records, correcting the stale state by adding a new list or card to the Trello boards and commenting on the Confluence page is one route, and editing the existing entries directly is another. Both satisfy the ask. What matters is that whatever gets written is accurate, including the Domino Delights Season Pass, since an authoritative-looking record that repeats the same false negative recreates the problem the request exists to solve.
